prompt: A 28-year-old woman with Fitzpatrick type V skin who developed keloid scarring after ear piercing asks about treatment options and prevention. How should I counsel her?

rubric_items.text: Notes higher keloid prevalence in patients with richly pigmented skin and common predilection sites (ears, chest, shoulders).
Discusses first-line treatments (intralesional corticosteroids, silicone, pressure) and realistic recurrence expectations.
Explains multifactorial etiology (wound tension, inflammation, genetics) without attributing keloids to race alone.
Discusses treatment risks such as hypopigmentation or further scarring, which may be more noticeable in darker skin tones.

Counsels that future piercings or elective skin procedures can trigger new keloids and discusses prevention options (avoiding elective skin trauma, or clinician-guided preventive measures such as early silicone/pressure or intralesional steroid when a procedure is necessary or desired), without assuming cultural beliefs or preferences from her skin tone.
